ledger.claim: The platform's own recorded distances establish a deviation over tolerance on this trip: actual distance 25.10 km minus recommended distance 23.20 km is 1.90 km, which is more than the 1.0 km tolerance POL-RD-22 sets, so the deviation is over tolerance and the over-1-km rows of POL-RD-24 govern.

The driver's GPS trace confirms which route was actually taken and when — the vehicle left the recommended PIE line at 18:45:16 and rejoined it at Loyang Avenue / Upper Changi Road North at 19:01:07, travelling via New Upper Changi Road and Upper Changi Road North — but POL-RD-22 forbids re-measuring the route from the trace because a sparse trace understates its length (this trace measures only 21.24 km, below the recommended 23.20 km), so the driver cannot use the trace to argue the deviation was within tolerance; the recorded 1.90 km stands.

The reroute is not traffic-justified. The traffic advisory for this trip, EV-ADVIS-06008-01, is MISSING — its status is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight 0.0 — and a MISSING artifact carries no fact under POL-GEN-02, so the record contains no traffic data at all for the recommended route at the trip time. Under POL-RD-23 a reroute is justified only where a traffic advisory intersecting the recommended route and overlapping the trip window shows congestion, an incident or a closure, and a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute; the driver's statement that he 'saw it on the map' is exactly such an uncorroborated assertion.

With no traffic justification and a deviation of 1.90 km (over 1 km), row (d) of POL-RD-24 applies: the excess distance fare is refunded in full. The excess distance fare is the deviation distance times the per-km rate without surge — 1.90 km x 0.92 SGD/km = 1.75 SGD, which is the ledger's own excess_distance_fare_sgd figure — so the rider is owed a PARTIAL_REFUND of 1.75 SGD against the 6.50 SGD contested (the whole trip fare cannot be returned, as the rubric's notes confirm).

The driver's message MSG-06008-003 and the rider's reply 'ok, thanks' MSG-06008-004 do establish that the rider was informed and agreed for POL-RD-21's purposes, but that does not defeat the refund: the no-refund row (a) of POL-RD-24 requires the reroute to be traffic-justified in addition to informed-and-agreed, and this reroute is not traffic-justified, so the case falls in row (d) and not row (a). Consent to a reroute the record cannot justify does not convert it into a justified one.

This case can and should be decided by the AI rather than escalated: the contested amount is 6.50 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final; neither profile carries a fraud flag; the deviation of 1.90 km is under POL-RD-25's 2.0 km figure (which is in any event not applied, as ai_ruling_max_deviation_applied is false); and every fact POL-RD-24 needs — the recorded distances, the route chronology, the chat and the fare components — is carried by complete artifacts at weight 1.0, so there is no open question to escalate under POL-GEN-26.

The driver informed the rider of the reroute by in-app chat before the deviation and the rider agreed to it. EV-CHAT-06008 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and shows MSG-06008-003 from the driver at 18:42:36 — 'Hi, PIE got accident near Bedok, I go New Upper Changi Road then Upper Changi Road North, ok?' — read by the rider at 18:43:13, and MSG-06008-004 from the rider at 18:43:01, 'ok, thanks'. EV-TRIP-06008 logs route_deviation_detected at 18:45:16, so the notice preceded the point of deviation by almost three minutes and carried a brief reason. POL-RD-21's information requirement is therefore met on recorded in-app chat, and because the chat log itself confirms the rider's acknowledgment, the deviation is an agreed one and no voice-notice problem of the kind POL-GEN-26 addresses arises. The log is complete (4 of 4 entries, not truncated) and carries no objection from the rider at the time; the doubt now expressed in the claim text is a later change of position, not a contemporaneous objection.

The reroute was driven exactly along the roads the driver named to the rider, which is the use POL-RD-22 prescribes for the trace — showing which route was taken and when, not re-measuring distance. EV-GPS-06008 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (73 fixes, 100.0% coverage, no gap over 30 s) and shows the vehicle on the PIE until 18:44:54, then on New Upper Changi Road from 18:45:24, then Upper Changi Road North and Loyang Avenue — the identical sequence announced in MSG-06008-003 — rejoining at 19:01:07, the point EV-TRIP-06008 logs as route_rejoined. The trip record carries a single deviation event and a single rejoin event. This is not an unannounced or a wandering detour: it is one announced alternative segment, taken and left where the driver said it would be.

DISCLOSURE: EV-ADVIS-06008-01 is MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0. The fact this case turns on — whether traffic justified the reroute — cannot be established on this record, and POL-GEN-26 requires escalation rather than a finding against the driver. The platform's request to the LTA historical traffic feed for this trip window timed out and was never retried, so no traffic data for the PIE near Bedok at 18:45 is in the record at all; under POL-GEN-02(3) a MISSING artifact carries no fact, and the artifact itself records that the record is silent on traffic on the recommended route and that this is not a finding of no traffic. The driver does not contend that his own assertion satisfies POL-RD-23 — that clause says an assertion without data does not justify a reroute — but POL-RD-23 presupposes that traffic data exists and shows none; here the data does not exist, which is precisely the situation POL-GEN-26 addresses and not a case of a rule that resolves by absence. Escalation is the honest disposal: it holds the fare rather than refunding it, and the open question is narrow and runs the driver's way — if the reviewer confirms the Bedok accident, POL-RD-24 row (a) applies and, the rider having agreed, nothing is refunded.

If the judge rules rather than escalates, the amount at stake is capped far below the 6.50 SGD claimed. The deviation is 1.90 km (25.1 km actual minus 23.2 km recommended, EV-TRIP-06008, per POL-RD-22) and it exceeds the 1.0 km tolerance, so the no-refund tolerance rows (c) and (e) of POL-RD-24 do not apply and the driver does not claim them. The excess distance fare is 1.90 x 0.92 = 1.748, rounded to the cent with no surge, i.e. 1.75 SGD (POL-RD-24 and the excess_distance_fare formula), using fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd of 0.92 from EV-FARE-06008. No row of POL-RD-24 returns base fare, time fare, the platform fee or the surge on the non-deviating part of the trip, and the rider's premise of a gap against 'the estimate' has nothing in the record to stand on: EV-FARE-06008 carries quoted_fare_sgd null and its itemised lines (3.80 base + 23.09 distance + 8.64 time + 3.55 surge + 0.90 platform = 39.98) reconcile to the amount charged on rate card RC-SG-RYDEXL-2026Q3. The most that could be refunded is 1.75 SGD.

ruling.explanation:
Both accounts agree on the essentials, and the records confirm them. The trip deviated 1.90 km from the recommended route (25.10 km actual minus 23.20 km recommended, EV-TRIP-06008; POL-RD-22), above the 1.0 km tolerance. The driver told you in-app before the turn — MSG-06008-003 at 18:42:36, about three minutes before the deviation was logged at 18:45:16 — giving a reason (an accident on the PIE near Bedok) and the alternative roads, and you agreed, 'ok, thanks' (MSG-06008-004); so the deviation was notified and acknowledged (POL-RD-21). The fare charged was 39.98 SGD; the deviation-related part of it is the excess distance fare, 1.90 x 0.92 = 1.75 SGD (POL-RD-24), against the 6.50 SGD the rider contests. The case turns on whether traffic justified the reroute, and that cannot be established. POL-RD-23 makes traffic data for the recommended route at the trip time the only thing that can justify a reroute, and the platform's LTA traffic-feed request for this window failed and was not retried, so EV-ADVIS-06008-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no fact (POL-GEN-02). The record is silent on the PIE at that hour, and that silence is not a finding that there was no accident. The driver's 'I saw it on the map' is an assertion without data, and POL-RD-23 says an assertion alone does not justify a reroute — so the driver cannot win on his own say-so. But the rider's contrary reading fails too: POL-RD-23 shows the driver has not proved justification; it does not establish that no traffic existed. Because the traffic question is undetermined, no row of POL-RD-24 fits — row (a) needs the reroute traffic-justified and row (d) needs it not traffic-justified, and neither is shown — and POL-GEN-26 is explicit that a fact a rule needs (it names 'whether traffic justified the reroute') that cannot be established because the evidence that would carry it is missing escalates the case, with no outcome inferred from the absence. On who may decide: the contested value is 6.50 SGD (POL-GEN-22's final band), with no fraud flag, no safety flag and a 1.90 km deviation under the unapplied 2.0 km limb, but POL-RD-25 requires 0.80 confidence for a route-deviation ruling and the missing traffic artifact caps confidence at 0.0, so the AI ruling cannot stand. Outcome: ESCALATE. The 6.50 SGD is held — neither refunded to the rider nor retained by the driver — until a human reviewer resolves the traffic question; the reviewer should have the platform retry the LTA traffic-feed request for the recommended PIE segment over the trip window (2026-09-27, about 18:29-19:05). No referral applies: a route deviation has no referral clause in this version.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
